Peach___Bacterial_spot.Environment: Warm temperatures (20–30°C), frequent rainfall, high humidity and strong winds promote disease development.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Spread: Spread through rain splash, wind-driven rain, contaminated pruning tools, infected nursery stock and plant debris.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Description: Bacterial Spot is a serious bacterial disease affecting peach trees. It damages leaves, fruits and young twigs, reducing fruit quality and market value. Severe infections may cause premature defoliation and reduced tree vigor.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small water-soaked lesions appear on young leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge, becoming dark brown with yellow halos. Fruits develop sunken spots.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves fall prematurely, fruits crack and twigs may develop cankers.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms usually appear within 7–14 days after infection under favorable conditions.

Treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides during dormant and early growing seasons.
Recommended_Actions: Inspect trees weekly during rainy periods.
Apply preventive copper sprays before disease spreads.
Maintain proper pruning and orchard hygiene.

Peach___healthy.Environment: Well-drained fertile soil, full sunlight (6–8 hours daily), balanced fertilization and proper irrigation.
Peach___healthy.Description: The uploaded peach leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease, pest infestation or nutrient deficiency. The tree appears healthy and capable of normal vegetative growth and fruit production.

Age_Cycle.Early: Healthy leaf emergence with normal green coloration.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Normal shoot growth and canopy development.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Continuous healthy growth throughout the growing season under proper orchard management.

Organic_Treatment: Maintain healthy soil with compost or well-decomposed manure.
Apply balanced organic fertilizers as needed.
Prevention: Inspect trees regularly for early disease symptoms.
Recommended_Actions: Inspect trees every week during the growing season.
Remove dead branches during routine pruning.
